# Power Transmission Device with Multiple Piston Configuration

## Overview

The present invention relates to a power transmission device that incorporates two or more pistons for its operation. This multi-piston configuration enables enhanced control and improved performance in the transmission of power between rotating components.

## Housing Structure

The device features a robust housing assembly formed by connecting several key components together to create a defined mounting space. Specifically, the housing is constructed by joining a clutch housing, a clutch connecting portion, a clutch hub, and a disk housing. These components work in concert to establish an enclosed mounting space that accommodates the internal operating mechanisms of the device.

## Piston Module and Hydraulic Operation

At the heart of the device is a piston module comprising multiple pistons, with each piston having its own corresponding piston chamber. Through the application of operating hydraulic pressure to these chambers, the piston module functions to selectively couple the first and second friction disks. This hydraulic actuation provides precise control over the engagement and disengagement of the friction elements, thereby governing the transmission of power through the device.

## Friction Disk Arrangement

The device employs two distinct sets of friction disks arranged in an alternating configuration. The first friction disks are splined to the interior surface of the disk housing, securing them to rotate with the housing assembly. In contrast, the second friction disks are splined to the exterior surface of the power transmission hub. These two sets of disks are arranged alternately with one another, creating an interleaved stack that maximizes the frictional contact area when the disks are engaged.

## Return Spring Mechanism

To ensure proper operation and disengagement, the device includes at least one return or separating spring. This spring provides a spring load that acts in opposition to the axial force generated by the operating hydraulic pressure. When hydraulic pressure is released, the spring load facilitates the separation of the friction disks and returns the pistons to their disengaged position, thereby ensuring reliable and consistent operation of the power transmission device.

# Multi-Piston Power Transmission Device

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to power transmission systems, and more particularly to a clutch-based power transmission device employing a multi-piston module for improved frictional engagement and enhanced transmission performance.

## Background

Conventional clutch-based power transmission systems typically rely on a single piston to apply axial force against a stack of friction disks. In such arrangements, the achievable clamping force and the precision of engagement are inherently limited by the size and stroke of the single actuating piston. As a result, these systems often struggle to deliver smooth, controlled engagement while simultaneously accommodating higher torque demands. There exists a need for a power transmission device that provides greater control over frictional engagement without requiring an impractical increase in the size of the actuating components.

## Summary of the Invention

This invention presents a power transmission device employing a multi-piston module, in which two or more pistons—each provided with a corresponding hydraulic chamber—act to selectively couple a set of alternating friction disks. These friction disks are arranged so that adjacent disks are alternately splined to a disk housing and to a power transmission hub, allowing torque to be transferred between the two components when the disks are pressed into frictional contact.

By distributing the actuating function across multiple pistons rather than concentrating it in a single piston, the device is able to generate a more evenly applied and readily controllable clamping force. Each hydraulic chamber can be pressurized to drive its associated piston axially against the friction disk stack, and the combined action of the pistons produces the total engagement force required for power transmission.

## Detailed Description

In a representative embodiment, the multi-piston module includes at least a first piston and a second piston, each seated within its own hydraulic chamber. When hydraulic fluid is supplied under pressure to the chambers, the pistons advance in the axial direction to compress the alternating friction disks. Because the friction disks are alternately splined—some to the disk housing and others to the power transmission hub—their frictional engagement establishes a rotational coupling that transfers power from the driving member to the driven member.

A key feature of the invention is the incorporation of return or separating springs. These springs are positioned to counteract the axial hydraulic force generated by the pistons. When hydraulic pressure is applied, the pistons overcome the spring bias to engage the friction disks. Conversely, when hydraulic pressure is reduced or released, the return springs urge the pistons back to their retracted positions, promptly separating the friction disks and disengaging the clutch.

The interplay between the hydraulic actuating force and the opposing spring force allows for a more finely modulated engagement characteristic. Rather than an abrupt, all-or-nothing coupling, the balance of forces enables gradual and controlled frictional engagement, reducing shock loads and wear on the friction surfaces. Moreover, the separating springs ensure clean and reliable disengagement, minimizing residual drag between the disks when the clutch is released.

## Advantages

By combining the distributed actuation of a multi-piston module with the counteracting force of return or separating springs, the device achieves several benefits:

- **Enhanced control:** The opposing spring force provides a predictable resistance against the hydraulic force, enabling more precise modulation of the engagement process.
- **Improved efficiency:** Controlled engagement reduces energy losses associated with slippage and heat generation, while positive disengagement minimizes parasitic drag.
- **Greater capacity in a compact form:** Multiple pistons deliver higher aggregate clamping force without necessitating a single oversized piston.
- **Reduced wear:** Smoother engagement and reliable separation extend the service life of the friction disks and associated components.

In this way, the invention enables more controlled and efficient frictional engagement, thereby improving the overall power transmission performance of clutch-based systems.

counterfactuals.output:
# SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a power transmission device configured to selectively transmit rotational torque between an input member and an output member. The device addresses limitations found in conventional clutch systems by providing improved engagement control, reduced actuation force requirements, and enhanced durability through a multi-piston actuation arrangement.

In accordance with one aspect of the invention, a power transmission device is provided that comprises a clutch housing assembly, two or more pistons disposed within the clutch housing assembly, a plurality of friction disks, and one or more return springs. The clutch housing assembly defines an interior chamber and provides a structural support for the operative components of the device while facilitating the transfer of torque between rotating members.

The two or more pistons are arranged to apply an axial clamping force to the friction disks in response to a supplied actuation pressure. By distributing the actuation load across multiple pistons, the device achieves a higher and more uniform engagement force while reducing the pressure demand on any individual piston. This multi-piston configuration enables more precise modulation of clutch engagement and disengagement, thereby improving the smoothness of torque transfer and reducing wear on the friction surfaces.

The plurality of friction disks are positioned within the clutch housing assembly and are configured to frictionally engage one another when compressed by the pistons. The friction disks selectively couple the input member to the output member, permitting the controlled transmission of torque when the disks are engaged and interrupting torque transmission when the disks are released.

The one or more return springs are operatively associated with the pistons and are configured to bias the pistons toward a disengaged position. Upon a reduction or removal of the actuation pressure, the return springs urge the pistons away from the friction disks, thereby releasing the clamping force and permitting rapid and reliable disengagement of the clutch. This arrangement ensures consistent return performance and helps prevent unintended residual engagement.

In operation, the actuation pressure acts upon the two or more pistons to compress the friction disks against a reaction surface within the clutch housing assembly, thereby coupling the input and output members for torque transmission. When the actuation pressure is relieved, the return springs restore the pistons to their initial positions, disengaging the friction disks and interrupting the torque path.

The present invention thus provides a compact, efficient, and durable power transmission device that offers improved engagement characteristics, reduced actuation requirements, and reliable disengagement. Additional features, aspects, and advantages of the invention will become apparent from the following detailed description, the accompanying drawings, and the appended claims.

counterfactuals.output:
# Summary of the Invention

The present invention relates to a multi-piston clutch power transmission device configured to selectively transmit rotational power between an input member and an output member with improved engagement precision, thermal management, and operational reliability.

In accordance with one aspect of the invention, the device comprises a generally cylindrical housing defining an internal chamber and having a first end adapted for coupling to a driving source and a second end adapted for coupling to a driven load. The housing includes one or more fluid ports in communication with the internal chamber to facilitate the selective delivery and evacuation of hydraulic fluid, and may further include cooling passages disposed about a peripheral wall thereof to dissipate heat generated during engagement and disengagement cycles.

In accordance with another aspect of the invention, a plurality of friction disks is disposed within the internal chamber of the housing. The friction disks comprise a first set of disks rotationally coupled to the input member and a second set of disks rotationally coupled to the output member, the disks of the first and second sets being interleaved in alternating relation such that axial compression of the friction disks establishes a torque-transmitting engagement therebetween, while axial separation of the friction disks interrupts the transmission of torque.

In accordance with a further aspect of the invention, a piston module is arranged within the housing and comprises a plurality of pistons disposed in a distributed arrangement and operable to apply a substantially uniform axial clamping force against the friction disks. Each piston is slidably received within a corresponding bore and is responsive to hydraulic fluid pressure delivered through the fluid ports, whereby actuation of the piston module urges the friction disks into engagement. The multi-piston arrangement distributes the applied clamping load across the friction surfaces, thereby reducing localized wear and promoting even engagement.

In accordance with yet another aspect of the invention, a plurality of springs is operatively associated with the piston module and biases the pistons toward a disengaged position, such that in the absence of sufficient hydraulic pressure the springs return the pistons and separate the friction disks, thereby interrupting power transmission. The springs may be configured as return springs, preload springs, or a combination thereof, to provide a predetermined baseline force and to ensure rapid and reliable disengagement upon reduction of fluid pressure.

Together, the housing, interleaved friction disks, distributed piston module, and biasing springs cooperate to provide a compact, durable, and responsive power transmission device capable of smooth engagement, efficient torque transfer, and reliable disengagement across a range of operating conditions. Additional features, aspects, and advantages of the invention will become apparent from the following detailed description, drawings, and appended claims.

counterfactuals.prompt: I'm working on a patent for an automotive clutch system with multiple pistons and friction disks. Can you generate a technical description of the device covering its main components?
counterfactuals.output:
# Multi-Piston Clutch System — Technical Description

Here's a technical description you can use as a starting framework. Note that patent claims and specifications benefit from professional patent attorney review before filing.

## Overview

The present invention relates to a clutch system for automotive applications, comprising a multi-piston actuation arrangement configured to engage and disengage a plurality of friction disks for selective torque transmission between an input member and an output member.

## Main Components

**1. Housing/Clutch Basket**
- A generally cylindrical housing defining an interior chamber
- Configured to receive and rotationally support the internal components
- May include mounting features for coupling to a transmission or engine

**2. Input Member (Drive Assembly)**
- Receives rotational torque from a prime mover (e.g., engine or motor)
- Rotationally coupled to a first set of friction disks

**3. Output Member (Driven Assembly)**
- Transmits torque to a downstream driveline component
- Rotationally coupled to a second set of friction disks

**4. Friction Disk Pack**
- A plurality of friction disks arranged in an alternating stack:
  - Drive disks (splined to the input member)
  - Driven disks (splined to the output member/hub)
- Friction surfaces may include organic, ceramic, or sintered materials

**5. Multi-Piston Actuation System**
- Two or more pistons arranged to apply axial clamping force to the disk pack
- Each piston movable within a corresponding cylinder/bore
- Actuation may be hydraulic, pneumatic, electromechanical, or a combination
- Multiple pistons allow for distributed or staged engagement force

**6. Return/Biasing Elements**
- Springs (e.g., diaphragm, coil, or wave springs) to return pistons to a disengaged position
- Ensures positive disengagement when actuation pressure is released

**7. Sealing Elements**
- Seals to maintain fluid pressure within actuation chambers

---

## A Few Clarifying Questions

To make this more precise and tailored, could you tell me:

1. **Actuation type** — Is it hydraulic, electromechanical, or another mechanism?
2. **Piston arrangement** — Are the pistons concentric, side-by-side, or serving separate disk packs?
3. **Purpose of multiple pistons** — Staged engagement, redundancy, torque capacity, or independent clutch control (e.g., dual-clutch)?
4. **Application** — Passenger vehicle, heavy-duty, EV, motorsport?
5. **What's novel** — What distinguishes your design from existing clutches? (This is the crux of a strong patent.)

---

**A note on patent strategy:** The strongest patents focus tightly on the *novel and non-obvious* features. A generic description like the above establishes context, but your claims should emphasize what makes your multi-piston arrangement unique. I'd recommend working with a registered patent attorney or agent for the formal filing.

Would you like me to expand any section or draft language once you share more details?

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a formal patent-style abstract describing a power transmission apparatus with a piston module containing two or more pistons that hydraulically couple alternating friction disks, along with counteracting return or separating springs.
counterfactuals.output:
# ABSTRACT

A power transmission apparatus comprising a piston module configured to selectively engage and disengage torque transmission between rotationally coupled members. The piston module includes two or more pistons arranged in operative communication with a hydraulic fluid supply, wherein said pistons are configured to hydraulically couple a plurality of alternating friction disks upon application of pressurized fluid. The friction disks comprise a first set of disks rotationally fixed to an input member and a second set of disks interleaved therewith and rotationally fixed to an output member, such that axial displacement of the pistons compresses the interleaved disks into frictional engagement to transmit torque therebetween. The apparatus further comprises one or more return or separating springs disposed in counteracting relation to the pistons, said springs biasing the pistons toward a disengaged position and urging the alternating friction disks apart upon reduction of hydraulic pressure. In this manner, the pistons and counteracting springs cooperate to provide controlled, reversible engagement of the friction disks, thereby enabling selective modulation of power transmission through the apparatus while ensuring positive disengagement and separation of the friction disks in the absence of applied hydraulic force.

# Hydraulic Clutch Power Transmission Device - Patent Claims

## Claim 1 (Independent Claim)

A hydraulic clutch power transmission device comprising:

**a) a housing** including:
- a clutch housing having a generally cylindrical configuration defining an interior chamber, said clutch housing having a first axial end and a second axial end;
- a clutch connecting portion integrally coupled to said clutch housing and extending radially inward therefrom, said clutch connecting portion configured to transmit rotational torque;
- a clutch hub disposed coaxially within said clutch housing and rotatably supported relative thereto, said clutch hub defining a plurality of external splines on an outer circumferential surface thereof; and
- a disk housing coupled to said clutch housing and defining a plurality of internal splines on an inner circumferential surface thereof;

**b) a first friction disk** having an inner peripheral edge engaging said external splines of said clutch hub such that said first friction disk is axially slidable relative to and rotationally fixed with respect to said clutch hub;

**c) a second friction disk** having an outer peripheral edge engaging said internal splines of said disk housing such that said second friction disk is axially slidable relative to and rotationally fixed with respect to said disk housing, said second friction disk being disposed in axially alternating relationship with said first friction disk to define a friction pack;

**d) a piston module** slidably received within said interior chamber of said clutch housing, said piston module defining a hydraulic pressure chamber between a rearward face of said piston module and an interior wall of said clutch housing, said piston module being axially displaceable in response to hydraulic fluid pressure introduced into said hydraulic pressure chamber to selectively compress said friction pack into frictional engagement; and

**e) a plurality of return springs** disposed in operative engagement with said piston module and biasing said piston module axially away from said friction pack toward a disengaged position when said hydraulic fluid pressure is reduced.

---

## Claim 2 (Dependent)

The hydraulic clutch power transmission device of Claim 1, wherein said clutch connecting portion comprises a radially extending annular flange integrally formed with said clutch housing, said annular flange defining a plurality of circumferentially spaced apertures for receiving fastening members.

## Claim 3 (Dependent)

The hydraulic clutch power transmission device of Claim 1, wherein said return springs comprise a plurality of coil compression springs arranged in a circumferentially spaced array about a rotational axis of said housing, each said coil compression spring seated between a spring retainer and said piston module.

## Claim 4 (Dependent)

The hydraulic clutch power transmission device of Claim 1, further comprising a pressure plate disposed adjacent said friction pack on a side opposite said piston module, said pressure plate providing a reaction surface against which said friction pack is compressed.

## Claim 5 (Dependent)

The hydraulic clutch power transmission device of Claim 1, wherein said piston module includes a piston body having an annular sealing member disposed on an outer circumferential surface thereof in sealing engagement with said interior chamber, thereby fluidically sealing said hydraulic pressure chamber.

## Claim 6 (Dependent)

The hydraulic clutch power transmission device of Claim 1, wherein said clutch hub and said disk housing are arranged for relative rotation such that engagement of said friction pack couples said clutch hub to said disk housing for common rotation and disengagement of said friction pack permits relative rotation therebetween.

## Claim 7 (Dependent)

The hydraulic clutch power transmission device of Claim 5, further comprising a balance chamber disposed on an axially opposite side of said piston body from said hydraulic pressure chamber, said balance chamber configured to receive fluid for counteracting centrifugal hydraulic pressure acting on said piston module.

## Claim 8 (Dependent)

The hydraulic clutch power transmission device of Claim 1, wherein said first friction disk comprises a steel plate and said second friction disk comprises a friction material bonded to a core plate, said first and second friction disks being alternatingly stacked.

---

*Note: These claims are illustrative examples of patent claim drafting style. For an actual patent application, engagement of a registered patent attorney or agent is recommended to ensure proper scope, novelty analysis, and compliance with applicable patent office requirements.*
